question: An engineer uses your Agent SDK tool to analyze a legacy billing module with Read, Grep, and Glob, building a shared understanding of its dependencies. The engineer then explored an extract-service refactoring and, later in the same session, an in-place cleanup refactoring. The cleanup proposals kept reusing assumptions from the extract-service exploration. Which change would best give each refactoring an independent start from the same analysis?

options.text: Start a fresh session for each refactoring and have the agent re-run the full dependency analysis of the billing module before exploring that refactoring.
options.reason: A fresh session discards the shared analysis baseline and repeats work that forking preserves for both branches.

options.text: Spawn a subagent through the Task tool for the cleanup refactoring, passing only the refactoring name in its prompt.
options.reason: Subagents do not inherit parent context, so this subagent would lack the dependency analysis that should be the shared baseline.

options.text: Use fork_session after the dependency analysis to create one branch per refactoring, each starting from the shared baseline.
options.reason: The guide names fork-based session management as the way to explore divergent approaches from a shared analysis baseline, keeping each branch isolated.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction telling the agent to disregard earlier refactoring explorations when it evaluates each new approach.
options.reason: The earlier exploration stays in the session context, so an instruction does not isolate the branches the way forking from a baseline does.
